title: Bootstrap admin password lifecycle broken: ADMIN_PASSWORD is silently ignored once any admin row exists, the docker-compose default makes the admin123 WARNING unreachable, and the SQLite file lives outside the mounted volume so container re-creation re-bootstraps the console with the published default
evidence: backend/cmd/server/main.go:164-169 — `func bootstrapAdmin(gdb *gorm.DB, cfg *config.Config) {` / `var count int64` / `gdb.Model(&model.AdminUser{}).Count(&count)` / `if count > 0 {` / `return` / `}`: once one admin exists, cfg.AdminPassword is never read again and nothing is logged. main.go:170-174 — `pass := cfg.AdminPassword` / `if pass == "" {` / `pass = "admin123" // 仅在未设置环境变量时默认，首次启动后必须修改` / `log.Println("[bootstrap] WARNING: using default admin password 'admin123'. Set ADMIN_PASSWORD to change.")`: the alert is gated solely on the empty string. docker-compose.yml:18 — `- ADMIN_PASSWORD=${ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin123}` makes that string non-empty on every compose start, so the branch is dead while bcrypt('admin123') (main.go:175) is still written; .env.template:28 — `ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin123` (uncommented). warnInsecureDefaults (main.go:187-194) checks only `cfg.JWTSecret == "change-me-jwt-secret"` and `cfg.MasterKey == "llm-router-guard-master-key"` — never the admin password. Persistence: config.go:62 — `DBDSN: getenv("DB_DSN", "gateway.db")` (relative), db.go:27 — `dialector = sqlite.Open(dsn)` (passed through unchanged, resolved against CWD), Dockerfile:25 — `WORKDIR /app` → /app/gateway.db, while docker-compose.yml:26 mounts only `- ${DATA_DIR_PATH:-./data}:/app/data`. Rotation cannot be recovered server-side: bootstrap is the only admin-provisioning path (routes.go:133-135 = GET /users, POST /users/:id/unbind-mfa, POST /users/:id/unlock; routes.go:45 PUT /auth/password requires the old password, auth.go:176). Password-only protection of the bootstrapped account: auth.go:86 `if sec.MFAEnabled && u.MFAEnabled` and settings.go:87 `return Security{MFAEnabled: true, MFARequiredAll: false, ...}`.
impact: Administrative account takeover through a provisioning defect, with no operator-visible signal at any stage. (1) The alert the project promises never fires on its documented Docker path: README.md:56 says first boot 'prints the default password to the console' and quickstart.en.md:47 says 'startup logs print a WARNING', yet with docker-compose.yml:18 injecting a non-empty value main.go:172-173 is unreachable — `docker compose up -d` on a host-exposed port (compose:10 `"${PORT:-8080}:8080"`) yields a console valid-login for admin/admin123 that logs nothing but `[bootstrap] created admin user: admin` (main.go:183). (2) Because cfg.AdminPassword's only consumer is the count==0 branch (whole-repo grep: config.go:66 producer, main.go:170 consumer), an operator who later sets a strong ADMIN_PASSWORD and restarts a persistent deployment — the form README:130-141 labels '(recommended)', which literally shows `ADMIN_PASSWORD="change-me" ./llm-router-guard` next to a surviving ./gateway.db — keeps the old credential with no log, no error, and no server-side check that a live login still uses the published default. (3) Because the DB is not in the mounted volume, any re-create (image upgrade, `down`+`up`, or simply editing .env and running `up -d`) destroys /app/gateway.db; db.go:63 AutoMigrate rebuilds an empty schema and bootstrapAdmin re-creates admin from the compose value, transparently restoring admin123 for an operator who had rotated away. The MFA second step does not cover any of this (a bootstrapped row has MFAEnabled=false and MFARequiredAll defaults false), and the 5-attempt lockout (auth.go:113-122) is meaningless against a known credential. A holder of the admin JWT reads provider upstream configuration, mints gateway API keys, exports full request/response audit, and toggles security settings.
mitigations_checked: bcrypt at DefaultCost on creation (main.go:175) and via the constant-time library helper on login (auth.go:76); `gorm:"uniqueIndex"` on Username (model.go:15); rotation endpoint exists (routes.go:45) and demands the old password (auth.go:176) plus an 8-char minimum (auth.go:166); no endpoint returns or resets a password without it; per-account lockout exists (auth.go:113-122) though authn-4 shows it is non-atomic; MFA is globally on by default (settings.go:87) but per-user opt-in so it does not protect the bootstrap account; TRUSTED_PROXIES/XFF and CORS are unrelated here. None of these address silent-ignore, silent-restore, or the suppressed warning. Additional supporting fact found during verification: the runtime image never ships the SPA — Dockerfile:26 copies only `/out/server` into /app and there is no go:embed anywhere in backend/, so MountStatic's auto-detect (routes.go:157-167) fails and returns without registering NoRoute → GET / is 404 under compose, meaning the documented remediation 'Change it immediately via the web UI' (README:56) is not even reachable in the deployment where the warning is suppressed.
corrected_facts: Cited line 166 is the Count() call; the ignore is decided by `if count > 0 { return }` at main.go:167-168 → corrected_line = 167.

The main.go:172 quote omits the inline comment `// 仅在未设置环境变量时默认，首次启动后必须修改`; the first-boot-only semantics are also documented (.env.template:25 '仅首次启动建号时生效', README:47-48), so 'silently' holds for logging/operator feedback, not for documentation.

Impact sub-claims (1) and (3) are mutually exclusive inside one compose run: editing .env and `docker compose up -d` is itself the re-create that wipes /app/gateway.db, so bootstrap applies the NEW password (data loss instead of a stale one); `docker restart`/host reboot keeps the writable layer (compose:27 `restart: unless-stopped`) and keeps the old hash. Both are reachable — just not in the same chain.
Sub-claim (3) does not immediately expose provider keys: a re-created instance starts empty; the exposure materialises once the operator re-provisions without rotating.
Cross-reference wording 'authn-3/authn-4 (no login throttling)' is imprecise: throttling exists at auth.go:113-122 but is per-account, non-atomic (authn-4) and irrelevant to a published default.
severity_rationale: high, not critical and not medium. Not critical: exploitation requires the operator to be sitting on an explicitly published default (README:48 'must be changed!') rather than a code-level authz bypass, and no unauthenticated code path yields RCE. Not medium: the combination of a live published credential + zero log output + no server-side default-credential detection + no admin reset path + a network-published port + the documented UI rotation path being absent from the image (Dockerfile:26) is a complete administrative-takeover chain that the code's own safety net (main.go:173) provably cannot fire in its flagship deployment form.
recommendation: Fail closed on the default: `ADMIN_PASSWORD=${ADMIN_PASSWORD:?set-admin-password}` in docker-compose.yml:18 (the pattern already used at README:287 for multi-node) or generate a random password and print it exactly once. Log an ERROR on any successful login whose bcrypt hash matches the published default (auth.go:76 path) and gate /api/admin/v1 on rotation. When bootstrapAdmin returns early (main.go:167), log `[bootstrap] ADMIN_PASSWORD ignored: N admin users already exist` instead of nothing, or reconcile deliberately. Ship the SQLite default inside the mounted volume (`DB_DSN=${DB_DSN:-/app/data/gateway.db}`) so re-creation cannot reset state, and fix the runtime image to copy web/dist so the documented UI rotation step exists.
exploit_sketch: 1) Operator follows quickstart.en.md §4 (`cp .env.template .env` — which carries `ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin123` at .env.template:28 — then `docker compose up -d`), no logs mention a default password. 2) Attacker: `curl -s -XPOST http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/auth/login -d '{"username":"admin","password":"admin123"}'` → 200 + 24h admin JWT (auth.go:110 → issueLogin auth.go:124-138; MFA step skipped because u.MFAEnabled is false). 3) `GET /api/admin/v1/providers` to read upstream endpoints/encrypted keys, `POST /api/admin/v1/apikeys` to mint a gateway key and proxy/spend quota, `GET /api/admin/v1/audit/calls` to read every prompt+response, `PUT /api/admin/v1/settings/security` to keep MFA off. 4) Silent-ignore variant: on the README:137-141 single-binary deploy with an existing ./gateway.db, set `ADMIN_PASSWORD=Str0ng…` and restart — login with admin123 still succeeds and nothing is logged (main.go:167-168). 5) Silent-restore variant: rotate via PUT /auth/password, then upgrade the image / `docker compose down && up -d` — /app/gateway.db is gone (not under the ./data mount), AutoMigrate rebuilds, and admin123 works again.
